exposure: Timing of planned cesarean delivery (37 vs. 35 gestational weeks)
cohort: 52 patients with prenatally diagnosed gastroschisis managed at the study institution between 2006 and 2014
finding: Planned cesarean delivery at 35 weeks gestation for fetuses with prenatally diagnosed gastroschisis was found to be safe, and patients delivered between 35 and 36.9 weeks had the best outcomes, including higher rates of primary closure, shorter time on mechanical ventilation and parenteral nutrition, and shorter hospital stays.
